subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: An atom of sodium has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. How many electrons does it have?
questions.explain: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons, so 11 electrons.

questions.q: Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?
options: They are made of free electrons
Strong electrostatic forces throughout a giant lattice
questions.explain: Strong electrostatic attractions in the giant ionic lattice need lots of energy to break.

questions.q: Approximately how many particles are in one mole of a substance (Avogadro's constant)?
A compound contains 0.2 mol carbon and 0.4 mol hydrogen. What is its empirical formula?
questions.explain: The ratio 0.2:0.4 simplifies to 1:2, giving CH2.

questions.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom concentrated?
options: In the empty space around the nucleus
questions.explain: Protons and neutrons in the nucleus contain nearly all the atom's mass.

questions.q: Why do simple molecular substances have low melting and boiling points?
questions.explain: Only weak intermolecular forces need to be overcome, not the strong covalent bonds.

questions.q: What is the concentration in mol/dm³ of a solution with 0.5 mol of solute in 2 dm³?
In a closed system, the total mass of the products of a reaction is:
questions.explain: Mass is conserved, so the products have the same total mass as the reactants.

questions.q: What is the formula of the compound formed from Mg²⁺ and Cl⁻ ions?
questions.explain: Two Cl⁻ ions balance one Mg²⁺ ion, giving MgCl2.

questions.q: Whose experiment led to the nuclear model of the atom, replacing the plum pudding model?
questions.explain: Ernest Rutherford's gold-foil (alpha-particle scattering) experiment showed the atom is mostly empty space with a small dense positive nucleus, replacing the plum pudding model.

questions.q: What is the relative charge of a proton?
questions.explain: Protons carry a relative charge of +1.

questions.q: Why is diamond unable to conduct electricity?
options: Its layers slide over each other
It has no charged particles free to move
questions.explain: In diamond every electron is held in a covalent bond, so none are free to carry charge.
